facebook.long_form:
🏁 RACE WEEK IS HERE — LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX 2026 🏁

The Formula 1 circus has arrived in Nevada, and tonight the action begins at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit.

Free Practice 1 and 2 are on the schedule for Thursday evening local time — the first time the cars hit the famously cold asphalt of the Las Vegas Strip this weekend. Qualifying follows on Friday night, with the race itself set for Saturday evening under the city lights.

This is Round 21 of 23 on the 2026 Formula 1 calendar, and while Kimi Antonelli has already clinched his historic first World Championship, the battle for second, third, and fourth in the Drivers' Standings is as close as it gets. Max Verstappen leads George Russell by just 17 points. Lewis Hamilton is 1 point behind Russell.

Three drivers. 18 points. 75 still to race. Las Vegas could not come at a better time.

Who do you think wins the Las Vegas Grand Prix? Drop your pick below 👇🏁

17 POINTS. 75 AVAILABLE. THIS IS WHY WE WATCH FORMULA 1.

Entering the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the Drivers' Championship fight for second place could not be closer:

🥈 Max Verstappen — 279 points
🥉 George Russell — 262 points
4️⃣ Lewis Hamilton — 261 points

Verstappen leads Russell by just 17 points. Hamilton is 1 point behind his own Mercedes teammate. Any three of them could emerge from Las Vegas with a dramatically different picture.

History adds another wrinkle. Russell won in Las Vegas in 2024. Verstappen has won here twice (2023 and 2025). Hamilton has never won on the Strip. All three have reasons to believe they can dominate this weekend.

What makes the Las Vegas GP so tantalizing is the volatility of a street circuit at night — safety cars, tire incidents, strategic pivots — any single variable can flip the standings. This is not a race to miss.

stories.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit — Tire Strategy, Cold Temps, and the Speed Trap

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Cold track. Three long straights. High-speed corners. The Las Vegas Strip Circuit rewards low-drag setups — but cold tires make life complicated. Mercedes thrives in these temps. This should be fascinating. #F1

facebook.long_form:
Not all street circuits are equal. The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is one of F1's most technically demanding layouts — and it's not because of the glamour.

Here's what the engineers are dealing with this weekend:

🌡️ COLD TEMPERATURES: Night racing on the Strip means track temperatures can drop significantly, slowing tire warm-up and dramatically affecting handling balance in the opening laps.

💨 THREE LONG STRAIGHTS: Teams must run low-drag setups to maximize straight-line speed — but that means less downforce through the high-speed corners, which demands more from the driver.

🏎️ TIRE DEGRADATION: The Las Vegas surface evolves over the weekend as rubber builds up. Session 1 (tonight) will tell teams a lot about which compound window they're working in.

Mercedes have historically been the team best able to extract performance from cold-track, high-speed circuits. The W17 is built to perform in exactly these conditions. Red Bull will need Verstappen to maximize qualifying in a car that may be at a slight disadvantage.

This is where F1 engineering meets chess. 🏆

What aspect of the Las Vegas GP do you find most fascinating — the racing, the city backdrop, or the technical puzzle? 👇

x_posts.text: Lando Norris won São Paulo two weeks ago from pole, 14.6 seconds clear. He arrives in Las Vegas as the in-form driver in the field. Can McLaren add win No. 4 on the Strip? #F1 #LasVegasGP

facebook.long_form:
Lando Norris arrives in Las Vegas on a high.

Just two weeks ago at the São Paulo Grand Prix, he led from pole position, dominated in difficult changing conditions, and won by 14.6 seconds. It was his third Formula 1 victory of the 2026 season — a campaign that has established him as one of the genuine stars of this era.

The 2026 McLaren MCL40 has been devastatingly quick in race trim this year, and while Norris sits sixth in the standings, McLaren as a team has shown the outright pace to challenge at any circuit on any given weekend.

Beside him is Oscar Piastri, the Australian quietly going about his business with five podiums to date. Piastri has identified Las Vegas as a circuit where McLaren's low-drag configuration could shine.

Can they add a fourth win to their 2026 tally? Saturday night could answer that question in spectacular fashion.

Who's your money on for the Las Vegas GP podium? 🏆👇

facebook.long_form:
📊 Charles Leclerc: 249 points. P5 in the standings.
📊 Lewis Hamilton: 261 points. P4 in the standings.

The gap is 12 points. With 75 points still on the table across three remaining rounds, Leclerc's fight for fourth place is very much alive.

For Ferrari, finishing inside the top-four of the Drivers' Championship would be a significant achievement in a season dominated by Mercedes and Kimi Antonelli. Leclerc's qualifying pace has been outstanding all year, and he's extracted multiple grid positions beyond what the SF-26's raw pace deserved.

Hamilton, now in his first season with the Scuderia in Ferrari red, has been adapting throughout the year and found his groove in the second half. He'll be motivated to protect fourth and show the paddock his value.

This subplot — Leclerc vs. Hamilton in the final three races — deserves as much attention as the Verstappen-Russell showdown.
